title: "Interventions and nets"

```{python}
#| include: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.style.use("styles/mint.mplstyle")
```

MINTverse models three vector-control levers, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs), indoor
residual spraying (IRS), and larval source management (LSM). Nets carry most of the
detail. A net choice and a resistance level have to be reduced to a single lethality
number before either package will look at them.

## Net types

ITNs are grouped into four formulations, and their names are the keyword arguments to
`calculate_dn0` and `Scenario`, as well as the allowed values of `net_type_future`.

| Name | Formulation | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `py_only` | Pyrethroid only | The baseline net |
| `py_pbo` | Pyrethroid with PBO | Restores kill in resistant populations |
| `py_pyrrole` | Pyrethroid with a pyrrole (chlorfenapyr) | Kill that does not decay with pyrethroid resistance |
| `py_ppf` | Pyrethroid with pyriproxyfen (PPF) | An effect on the next generation, folded into `lsm` |

The long forms are the canonical values, and `net_types()` returns them alphabetically,
which puts `ppf` before `pyrrole`. Indexing into the list rather than naming the net is
therefore a common source of error.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from estimint import calculate_dn0, net_types

net_types()
```

The short aliases are accepted everywhere the long forms are.

## Net effectiveness and dn0

A net's effect on transmission is summarised by `dn0`, the probability that a mosquito
is killed when it contacts a treated net. The value depends on the insecticide and on
the resistance level.

`calculate_dn0` takes a resistance level and a net mix, and returns the usage-weighted
`dn0` along with the total coverage.

```{python}
mix = calculate_dn0(0.5, py_only=0.4, py_pbo=0.2)
mix
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## `itn_use` is already the total coverage

`DN0Result.itn_use` is the **sum of the shares you passed**, which here is 0.4 + 0.2 =
0.6. It is not a scaling factor waiting to be applied. Multiplying it by a usage figure a
second time halves the coverage, which lowers the modelled protection and raises the EIR
the setting is judged to need. No warning is issued when this happens.
:::

## How resistance affects each net

Setting usage to 1.0 for one net type at a time and sweeping resistance from 0 to 1
gives the resistance response of each formulation on its own terms.

```{python}
nets = ["py_only", "py_pbo", "py_pyrrole", "py_ppf"]
resistance = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 41)

dn0 = pd.DataFrame(
    {net: [calculate_dn0(r, **{net: 1.0}).dn0 for r in resistance] for net in nets},
    index=pd.Index(resistance, name="resistance"),
)

dn0.loc[[0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]].round(4)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Probability a mosquito dies on contact with a net (`dn0`), against pyrethroid resistance, for each net type at full usage."
#| fig-alt: "Four declining curves of dn0 against resistance from 0 to 1. Pyrrole is highest throughout, starting near 0.56 and staying flattest before falling away past 0.75. PBO starts near 0.51 and PPF near 0.41; the two converge at high resistance and cross at about 0.92, after which PPF is the higher of the two. Pyrethroid-only is lowest throughout, starting near 0.34 and falling to zero at full resistance."
fig, ax = plt.subplots()

for net in nets:
    ax.plot(dn0.index, dn0[net], label=net)

ax.set_xlabel("Pyrethroid resistance")
ax.set_ylabel("dn0 (probability of death on contact)")
ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
ax.set_ylim(0, None)
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

Four features of the curves bear on procurement. The first is that the best and the worst
net do not change. The pyrrole net is the most lethal at every resistance level, and
pyrethroid-only is the least lethal at every resistance level. Neither ranking depends on
the local resistance, so a pyrrole net is never the wrong choice on effectiveness grounds
and a pyrethroid-only net is never the right one.

PBO and PPF swap places at high resistance. PBO is the better of the two up to about 0.92
resistance, above which PPF overtakes it. The crossover sits at the extreme end of the
range and rarely decides a procurement, but it is a reason not to read the ordering of
the middle two nets off a single number.

The gap also widens with resistance. At zero resistance a pyrrole net is worth about 1.7
times a pyrethroid-only net, while by 0.75 it is worth more than twice as much. The case
for a next-generation net is weakest exactly where resistance is low.

Fourth, the decline is steep at the far end. All four curves fall away sharply after
declining gently to about 0.75. Pyrethroid-only reaches zero at full resistance, and the
other three retain a residual kill. A setting at 0.9 resistance sits in the steep part of
the curve, where a small error in the resistance level you supply produces a large error
in `dn0`.

The resistance-to-`dn0` curves come from the same published source that
`malariasimulation` uses.

## IRS and LSM

IRS coverage enters as `irs_use` for the present and `irs_future` for the campaign being
evaluated. LSM enters as `lsm`. Both are coverage proportions on a 0 to 1 scale, and
neither has a `dn0`-style effectiveness term, so the coverage itself is the input.

PPF nets interact with LSM, because `run_scenarios` folds PPF coverage into the LSM term
before the emulator runs.

$$
\texttt{lsm\_eff} = \min\big(\texttt{py\_ppf} \times 0.248 + \texttt{lsm},\ 1.0\big)
$$

So a scenario with PPF nets at 0.5 coverage and LSM at 0.30 reaches the emulator with
an effective LSM of $0.5 \times 0.248 + 0.30 = 0.424$.

::: {.callout-important}
## The `lsm` you get back is not the `lsm` you passed

The `lsm` column in the `run_scenarios` output is `lsm_eff`, after the PPF
contribution has been added. If you are reconciling a scenario's inputs against its
outputs, or diffing two scenarios, this is the column that will not match. The 0.248 is
why.
:::

## What dn0 does not capture

`dn0` summarises the probability of death on contact, and nothing else. It does not
capture **repellence**. Neither the protection that repellence gives nor the diversion of
biting it produces is anywhere in the number.

Nor does it capture **attrition**. A net mix is a snapshot at the decision point, and
`dn0` and `itn_use` are held constant across the whole trajectory. A campaign's
protection is modelled as arriving in full at day 3285 and holding.

A single mix is also assumed to apply across the whole population. A district where half
the villages have new nets and half have five-year-old nets is not the same as a district
uniformly in the middle, but that is how it will be represented.

The resistance level you supply should be the local pyrethroid resistance at the
decision point. Given the steepness of the curves above 0.75, vary it in a sensitivity
check rather than trusting a single value.
